content.summary_of_the_paper: To address the task of Few-Shot Domain Adaptation Object Detection (FSDAOD), this paper mainly proposes two modules: 1) Instance-level Prototype learning Network (IPNet) and 2) Feature-level Spatial Attention Transfer (FSAT) for improved performance. The IPNet is proposed to fuse instances from both domains to learn the domain-invariant prototypical representations. FSAT is used to decouple the foreground and background for both target and source data.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
+ Embedding the meta-learning into the typical adversarial adaptation process is interesting for FSDAOD.


Weakness:

- The design of the model is not well-motivated.

1) the domain gap between target and source is usually the main point to decrease the generalization of the model. However, both the proposed IPNet and FSAT do not directly address the domain shift or use any domain loss. I feel like fusing two domain features brutally will still suffer from domain shift when using the prototyping.  Only the task of the few-shot challenge is addressed here.

2) The idea of using FSAT for separating foreground and background is not well-motivated. Does this module aim to address the issue of missing detection or learn a better representation for feature encoder? Looks like this module is only to regularize the training of feature extractor like ResNet101 or VGG16 with prototypes from IPNet? It would be also good to explain why RPN is not trained in both of the two modules if this is the case.

3) FSAT is using adversarial learning for foreground and background instead of source or target. While this learning process may help to address the domain gap without aligning the distribution between source and target, would the inherent domain shift affect the performance of the foreground/background separation? 

4) Since we only have few labeled target images and many source images, the issue of data imbalance will be taking place in this model. Will the imbalance of source and target images affect the model? I see only the focal loss applied for boxes imbalance issue.

* Lack of analysis:
1) The idea of prototyping in IPM is not new and does not have further revision or customized for cross-domain tasks. Obviously, directly fusing two data would suffer from the domain gap. For example, does the improvement come from seeing few labeled data from the target or the model is really addressing the domain gap?
2)How would separating foreground and background be effective for domain shift is missing. 

* Missing context
1) The setting of few-shot cross-domain object detection is not strictly defined well. For example, CDOD assumes the labels of target domains are unavailable. Here FSCDOD can access the labels from the target domain.
2) Many recent DAOD related works in CVPR are missing. For example:

[a] He, Mengzhe, Yali Wang, Jiaxi Wu, Yiru Wang, Hanqing Li, Bo Li, Weihao Gan, Wei Wu, and Yu Qiao. "Cross Domain Object Detection by Target-Perceived Dual Branch Distillation." In Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)., pp. 9570-9580. 2022.

[b]Zhao, Liang, and Limin Wang. "Task-specific Inconsistency Alignment for Domain Adaptive Object Detection." In Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), pp. 14217-14226. 2022

[c] Li, Yu-Jhe, Xiaoliang Dai, Chih-Yao Ma, Yen-Cheng Liu, Kan Chen, Bichen Wu, Zijian He, Kris Kitani, and Peter Vajda. "Cross-Domain Adaptive Teacher for Object Detection." In Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)., pp. 7581-7590. 2022

[d] Wu, Jiaxi, Jiaxin Chen, Mengzhe He, Yiru Wang, Bo Li, Bingqi Ma, Weihao Gan, Wei Wu, Yali Wang, and Di Huang. "Target-Relevant Knowledge Preservation for Multi-Source Domain Adaptive Object Detection." In Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)., pp. 5301-5310. 2022.

[e] Li, Wuyang, Xinyu Liu, and Yixuan Yuan. "SIGMA: Semantic-complete Graph Matching for Domain Adaptive Object Detection." In Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR). 2022.

[f] Xu, Yunqiu, Yifan Sun, Zongxin Yang, Jiaxu Miao, and Yi Yang. "H2FA R-CNN: Holistic and Hierarchical Feature Alignment for Cross-Domain Weakly Supervised Object Detection." In Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)., 2022.


* Minor comments
1) Figure 2 is not clear for IPM. Does the class-wise average only apply to the support set? If so, what is the process for the query set (red features). This is missing in the figure.

2) In figure 2, since global average pooling is also performed aligned with class, is it the same as class-wise average? Why use two different names?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is unclear in many parts (see weakness). Considering it may be trivial to apply FSOD model directly to FSCDOD without further design process, novelty is also a concern for this paper. Reproducibility is not sure.
content.summary_of_the_review: The proposed two modules are not well-motivated to the FSCDOD setting and there are many unclear parts in the paper (see weakness). The current version is obviously not ready for publication.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper studies the FS-DAOD problem with the prototypical meta-alignment and foreground-aware adversarial learning in a step-by-step manner. Extensive experiments are conducted on some benchmarks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. The paper well clarifies its method.
2. The experiments are comprehensive.

Weakness:
1. I am not convinced by the motivation, which is the confusion in between-class and foreground attention. Though the samples in the target domain are much less than that in the UDA setting, they equip with loose labels. The labels in those settings like k-shots offer accurate classification and foreground information. For example, in Table 1, simply using TFA to fine-tune on 1-shot achieves 35.9 mAP, +10.3% compared with source-only. Whether FS-DAOD is worse than UDA is not certain. There should be some experiments to verify the motivation.
2. The novelty is limited. Since meta learning and adversarial learning are quite popular in FSOD and DAOD, respectively, the novelty is not enough. Moreover, using foreground area as attention on adversarial loss is not new in the community [1].
3. In Table 1, SWDA is conducted with the FUDA setting, which is not fair compared with both UDA and FDA. SWDA in the FDA setting by simply using target detection loss should be reported.
4. In Table4, the result of SWDA is not equipped with Cyclegan according to the original paper. The experiment setting might be not fully aligned.

[1] Zheng Y, Huang D, Liu S, et al. Cross-domain object detection through coarse-to-fine feature adaptation[C]. Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF conference on computer vision and pattern recognition. 2020: 13766-13775.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Good clarity. Fair quality. Poor Novelty. And I am not sure about the reproducibility.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper tackles the FS-DAOD problem by a combination of meta-learning and adversarial learning, which is lack of novelty. Its motivation is not certain enough.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The author identified a new task: few-shot domain adaptation object detection, proposed a method combining prototype based meta learning feature alignment and feature map refinement by adversarial training, and achieved state-of-the-art results on the few-shot domain adaptation settings.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The proposed task focuses on object detection. But 2 of the 4 benchmarks only contain 1 class. This is not usual in a detection task. It is better to evaluate different methods on more general detection tasks.

There are also ambiguities of the method itself:
1. In Sec 3.1, F and I are mentioned but not used. And the meaning of "feature-level" and "instance-level" is not clear.
2. In Eq. (8), $L_p$ is only the triplet loss between query samples, does it mean we do not need support set? If so, the whole process is not meta learning any more, and the whole Section 3.2.1 makes no sense.
3. In Sec 3.3, there are 3 stages of training. However, it is not clear which part of the detection model is trained in each stage.
4. Table 6 compared CE loss and Triplet loss in IPM, but it is not clear what the CE loss is.
5. Still in Table 6, the improvement of BG align upon FG is similar to that of CE and triplet. Why is the conclusion different? We choose Triplet over CE, while use both FG and BG together.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The clarity problems are covered in weaknesses.

Novelty is ok. The author proposed a new task, provided a novel method to solve the task. Although each of the technique is not new, the combination of them is a good solution to the problem. But the evaluation of the proposed task can be improved (see weaknesses)

Reproducibility can not be evaluated. Code is not available.
content.summary_of_the_review:
The main problem is the evaluation dataset. As a new detection task, it is weird to propose benchmarks with only one class. This will significantly limit the importance of the task. 

Another concern is the clarity of the method. As discussed in weaknesses, some detail of the method is not clear. I will raise my rating, if the authors can answer my questions.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
